(UAE)[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Monarchies_in_Asia&action=edit&section=3 "Edit section: United Arab Emirates (UAE)")]The [United Arab Emirates](/wiki/United_Arab_Emirates "United Arab Emirates") is a consisting of [7 emirates](/wiki/Emirates_of_the_United_Arab_Emirates "Emirates of the United Arab Emirates"), each ruled by [absolute monarchs](/wiki/Absolute_monarchs "Absolute monarchs"). The [President](/wiki/President_of_the_United_Arab_Emirates "President of the United Arab Emirates"), [Vice President](/wiki/Vice_President_of_the_United_Arab_Emirates "Vice President of the United Arab Emirates") and [Prime Minister](/wiki/List_of_prime_ministers_of_the_United_Arab_Emirates "List of prime ministers of the United Arab Emirates") are elected by the [Federal Supreme Council](/wiki/Federal_Supreme_Council "Federal Supreme Council"), which consists of the [rulers of the seven emirates](/wiki/List_of_rulers_of_individual_Emirates_of_the_United_Arab_Emirates "List of rulers of individual Emirates of the United Arab Emirates"). However, in practice, the office of President is traditionally held by the [Ruler of Abu Dhabi](/wiki/Ruler_of_Abu_Dhabi "Ruler of Abu Dhabi"), while the offices of Vice President and Prime Minister are held by the [Ruler of Dubai](/wiki/Ruler_of_Dubai "Ruler of Dubai"). states](/wiki/Princely_states "Princely states")The British ruled [Indian Empire](/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj") became independent from British rule in 1947 and became the [Dominion of India](/wiki/Dominion_of_India "Dominion of India") and the [Dominion of Pakistan](/wiki/Dominion_of_Pakistan "Dominion of Pakistan") and in 1950 India became the [Republic of India](/wiki/India "India"), in 1956 Pakistan became the [Islamic Republic of Pakistan](/wiki/Pakistan "Pakistan"), and in 1971 the province of [East Pakistan](/wiki/East_Pakistan "East Pakistan") separated from Pakistan to become [Bangladesh](/wiki/Bangladesh "Bangladesh"). Princely states were only in the present-day countries of India and Pakistan, and not Bangladesh. The princely states who were vassal states of the British, had a certain degree of power and autonomy during the [British Raj](/wiki/British_Raj "British Raj"). The princely states had integrated into the newly independent India and Pakistan between 1947 and 1975 (the majority of states ascended into India or Pakistan in 1948) and the former monarchs of the princely states who joined before 1971 in India and before 1972 in Pakistan became titular rulers that received a [privy purse](/wiki/Privy_Purse_in_India "Privy Purse in India") and initially retained their statuses, privileges, and autonomy. During this time, the former princely states in India were merged into unions, each of which was headed by a former ruling prince with the title of *Rajpramukh* (ruling chief), equivalent to a state governor.[[2]](#cite_note-2)In 1956, the position of *Rajpramukh* was abolished and the federations dissolved, the former principalities becoming part of Indian states. The states which acceded to Pakistan retained their status until the promulgation of a new constitution in 1956, when most became part of the province of [West Pakistan](/wiki/West_Pakistan "West Pakistan"); a few of the former states retained their autonomy until 1969 when they were fully integrated into Pakistan. The Indian Government formally derecognised the princely families in 1971, followed by the Pakistani Government in 1972, in which their titles, autonomy, and privy purses were take away.
